findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so log calls through it are lost
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. `LoggerMiddleware` now always logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. As a result, any test that injects a `TestLogger` and asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`, `Message` or `Ctx` will always see zero calls, because the call was recorded on a throwaway instance. Return `f`, or a logger that shares its recorded state, so the fake keeps recording when used through `FromContext`.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks other implementations
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is a new method on the widely used `plugins/log.Logger` interface. Every implementation outside the two updated here must now implement it or fail to compile. That includes other fakes and test loggers in the repo, enterprise code and external consumers. Check all implementers, or use a separate optional interface with a type assertion.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the FromContext wiring
findings.body: The pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname fields used to be added explicitly by `LoggerMiddleware`. They now depend on two things: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` setting contextual attributes, and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` picking them up. The traceID field likewise now relies only on the contextual log provider. Nothing tests this path. If the middleware is reordered, or the type assertion in `FromContext` falls back to `d.New()`, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines would silently lose these fields. Add a test that checks the contextual attributes are present on the logged request.
